lead: the hospital had your number before you knew you were on the form, and the woman reading it out to you assumed the arrangement was years old, made in a conversation that has never happened.
sun: nothing about you has needed revising in nineteen years: one number, the rent clearing on the second of the month, a phone answered at any hour. a form will take that and will not take warmth. so the blank line gets filled in with you, in kitchens you have never sat in, by people working out who would turn up if the worst arrived on a wednesday. what gets written down is a load path.
moon: nothing was asked of you, and that is the mechanism rather than an oversight. a blank line is not a request. it offers room, and room of that quality gets used by whoever finds it, so seventeen people have written you into theirs, each believing the arrangement predates them — that you were already the person for this, and they were recording something.
pull: a blank line does not ask, and neither did they. you are what seventeen households have written down for the worst night of their lives, learned each time from a stranger on a phone.
tension: you cannot decline any of it, since declining needs the conversation that was never held, and starting one now means telling somebody you have been keeping count. no list exists either. how many forms carry your number is not a figure anybody holds, including you — it went up again last spring, and you found out the way you always do, from a voice using your name and relying on it already.
cost: the call that comes before dawn finds you dressed and driving inside twelve minutes, for a household you have sat in twice. your own form has your sister's number on it from before she moved twice, and correcting it has never seemed worth a phone call — being the one they would all ring supplies no impulse at all to arrange one for yourself.

lead: a person who has told nobody in their actual life types it out to two thousand strangers, and the only reason that works is a set of terms one person has enforced identically since the beginning.
sun: what you put up is a set of terms, applied the same way for twenty-two years: who is inside, what happens to a person who repeats something elsewhere, and how fast it happens. it has not bent for anyone, including people you like. that is the entire engineering — a place where the same thing happens every time is a place where somebody will eventually type the actual sentence.
moon: you read all of it, and the reading does not switch off when the laptop shuts. a change in somebody's punctuation tells you a marriage has gone, weeks before the paragraph about it arrives. carrying that is not hard in any way you could point at; it simply accumulates, inside a person the two thousand of them do not experience as a person.
pull: people tell a room things they will not tell a person. you are the room, you remember all of it by name, and the arrangement has no channel that runs the other direction.
tension: the one time you wrote a line about your own year, the place treated it as an announcement: everybody replied, carefully, and the ordinary traffic stopped for nine days. a wall that says something is an event, and events are not what people come there for. the terms went on holding afterwards. everything anyone in there knows about you fits in a username and the date the archive starts at.
cost: spotting the person in real trouble takes you a fortnight less than it takes their own family, off a shift in how somebody signs off. outside the terms, none of it exists: what you hold cannot be used, mentioned, or taken to anybody, and the people whose worst years you carried in full would not recognise your voice in a shop.

lead: twice a day since before either child was born, the yard fills with the same sound at the same minute, and the houses on that road have quietly set their own hours by a clock that is a person.
sun: the parlour, the tracks, the collection bay: you put all of it up thirty-one years ago and nothing has been altered since, because it was right. a cycle that never varies is a structure — it has an inside, and the inside is a herd, a family and a haulage schedule that all run at the pitch you set. nobody arranges their day around a preference. they arrange it around something that holds.
moon: the beat goes out twice a day and everything within a mile takes a fix from it: the tanker, the relief man, the school run. reading what returns is how you would know where you are, and a sound that has not varied since you set it gives the same figure every time. their positions are exact. yours is not measured by anything.
pull: half the road knows what time it is because of a noise you make twice a day, and nothing that returns from it has ever told you one thing about how you are doing.
tension: a hard year has nowhere in the day to appear. the parlour runs at quarter past five on the morning after bad news, and the tanker comes on the same afternoon either way, so nothing about your state ever reaches a surface where somebody could read it off you. the regularity gets taken for contentment by people who love you, and you cannot correct them, because the only instrument you own puts out the same number every day.
cost: nothing has been late in thirty-one years — not a milking, not a collection, not one appointment with the vet — through two bereavements and a hip replaced twice. asked directly how the last decade has been, the answer available to you is the yield figures, which are excellent, and the fact that the cycle has not slipped, which is not an answer about a person.

lead: you had the sentence ready before they arrived and you said it once, at the table: stay as long as you need. nine years on, what that sentence turned into is holding up part of the roof.
sun: inside a month the offer had become fittings. a key cut, a name added to the utility account, a shelf up in the hall where their post goes, the car arrangement written into how the week works. that is the only way you know how to hold something: you put it up properly, and an offer that gets built is not an offer any more. it is where the room is.
moon: the offer was a real event and everybody involved can date it — the wording thought about beforehand, the evening chosen, the saying of it costing something. it was also the last thing in the arrangement that happened. everything since holds, and a thing that holds does not occur, so no second evening has come round on which the room could be accepted again, refused, or given up.
pull: the offer took one sentence and nine years have gone up on top of it. an offer can be accepted or declined; what they are living in now can only be demolished.
tension: you have one spare room and it stopped being spare almost at once. since then a cousin and a friend after the fire have needed exactly what you gave once, and the sentence you are known for is one you no longer have available. what you did is described in the present tense by people who admire it, and all of it comes from one evening that is holding, which is the same reason it cannot happen twice.
cost: you can put a person with nothing inside an arrangement that will hold for a decade — no probation, no review, nothing to reapply for. what you have not had since is a guest. people either become part of the structure by the second month or were never coming, and nothing in your life now is a thing anybody gets to leave at the end of.
